verdicts.reason: A keeps a clear text-left/product-right banner, but the bold attribution is larger than the quote it credits, and the logo floats off the text's left edge. B shrinks the quote to small text that leaves 'soon.' alone on a line, places the attribution on the edge of the circle, and turns the logo into a tiny, broken-looking 'SOLST CE' at bottom centre.

A shrinks the product to a small can whose label can't be read, stranded on the left. The quote mark sits far above its quote, and the text runs into the circle's edge. B keeps the product as the hero, but its attribution is bolder than the quote and its logo is misaligned with the left text edge.

The two are nearly the same layout. In A the product is sized to sit within the circle with more breathing room, but the logo is very small and misaligned with the quote. In B the product is oversized and crowds the top edge. Both keep the problem of an attribution that outweighs the quote.

A shrinks the product to a meaningless icon beside a tiny logo at the bottom, which loses the key imagery, and its quote leaves 'too soon.' as an orphaned line. B keeps the product and a clear split layout, though its attribution outweighs the quote and its logo placement is arbitrary.
